title: India Successfully Tests Kusha Long-range Surface-to-Air Missile
gist: India's DRDO conducted the maiden flight test of the M1 long-range surface-to-air missile on July 23 from APJ Abdul Kalam Island off Odisha, intercepting an electronic target simulating a high-speed, high-altitude threat. M1 is one of three interceptors in the Kusha program, which underpins a multi-layered long-range air defense architecture targeted for completion by 2035 under Mission Sudarshan Chakra.

insights.claim: India's Defense Research and Development Organization successfully conducted the maiden test of the M1 long-range surface-to-air missile on July 23 from APJ Abdul Kalam Island off the Odisha coast.
insights.so_what: First-flight success moves an indigenous long-range SAM from paper to program, reducing India's dependence on imported air-defense systems.
